items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Given a rational matrix G with complex coefficients and a domain $\Gamma$ in the closed complex plane, both arbitrary, we develop a complete theory of coprime factorizations of G over $\Gamma$, with denominators of McMillan degree as small as possible. The main tool is a general pole displacement theorem which gives conditions for an invertible rational matrix to dislocate by multiplication a part of the poles of G. We apply this result to obtain the parametrized class of all coprime factorizations over $\Gamma$ with denominators of minimal McMillan degree n
                    <jats:sub>b</jats:sub>
                    ---the number of poles of G outside $\Gamma$. Specific choices of the parameters and of $\Gamma$ allow us to determine coprime factorizations, as for instance, with polynomial, proper, or stable factors. Further, we consider the case in which the denominator has a certain symmetry, namely it is J all-pass with respect either to the imaginary axis or to the unit circle. We give necessary and sufficient solvability conditions for the problem of coprime factorization with J all-pass denominator of McMillan degree n
                    <jats:sub>b</jats:sub>
                    and, when a solution exists, we give a construction of the class of coprime factors. When no such solution exists, we discuss the existence of, and give solutions to, coprime factorizations with J all-pass denominators of minimal McMillan degree (>n
                    <jats:sub>b</jats:sub>
                    ). All the developments are carried out in terms of descriptor realizations associated with rational matrices, leading to explicit and computationally efficient formulas.
                  </jats:p>
title: Minimal Degree Coprime Factorization of Rational Matrices

items.abstract: <jats:p>For the OEIS sequence A177265 (the number of permutations of {1,. .. , n} having exactly one string of consecutive fixed points), R. J. Mathar contributed on 1 July 2022 the conjectured order-4 P-recursive recurrence a(n)-(n-1)a(n-1)-(n-1)a(n-2) + (n-1)a(n-3) + (n-2)a(n-4) = 0, n ≥ 5, which has remained unproven on the OEIS entry. We prove it. In fact we show something stronger: a(n) satisfies the previously unrecorded order-3 recurrence (n-1) a(n)-(n2-n1) a(n-1)-n a(n-2) + n(n-1) a(n-3) = 0, n ≥ 4, and that Mathar's order-4 recurrence is an immediate algebraic consequence of this order-3 recurrence: it equals the sum of the order-3 recurrence evaluated at n and at n-1, divided by (n-1). The order-3 recurrence is derived directly from the combinatorial definition of a(n) together with the classical derangement recurrence D(n) = n D(n-1) + (-1)ⁿ; the proof is entirely self-contained and relies on no unproved OEIS comment.</jats:p>
title: A Short Proof of Mathar’s 2022 Recurrence Conjecture for Oeis A177265, via a new Order-3 Recurrence

items.abstract: <jats:p>With the steady growth of the population in our country, the analysis of population is essential to the distribution of social resources and the improvement of the population quality. In this paper, we use the neural network of rational spline weight functions with cubic numerator and quadratic denominator to establish the model of Chinese population by four indicators, gender ratio, birth rate, elderly dependency ratio and natural increase rate. Finally we come to the conclusion through MATLAB simulation that the training speed is fast and the error is small. This kind of neural network can be applied to population analysis and it could be used in various fields.</jats:p>
title: Population Analysis Based on Neural Network of Rational Spline Weight Functions with Cubic Numerator and Quadratic Denominator
